author: Mark Atwood
text:
DONE, and the bead was stale by the time I read it. It says "the agent's
loopback endpoint serves no JMAP WebSocket"; it does, and has since commit
a46c5dbe:

- crates/mimid-agent/src/http.rs routes GET /jmap/ws
  (`get_websocket`/`websocket`), behind the same bearer credential as every
  other route, with the Session advertising RFC 8887's capability and
  supportsPush false.
- crates/mimid-agent-jmap/src/vtc_stream.rs is option 1 of the three this
  bead ranked: a `CallSignals` extension handler that follows the store's
  change feed for Change::CallSignal and pushes each one as a
  VTCCallSignal, started by VTCStreamEnable, with the Parlor-shaped care
  the bead asked for (a second enable replaces the first subscription and
  the task reading for it; a lagged receiver ends the stream rather than
  half-connecting, because a missed signal is a negotiation that will not
  complete and there is nothing to re-read).

Option 2 (carry signals over the EventSource) was correctly not taken: it
would have extended RFC 8620's event stream with our own event type.

WHAT WAS STILL MISSING was the other end of the same problem, and it is
fixed in 87c35f37 (bead mimid-1wgh.114.2): the VTC methods were not
registered and the capability was not advertised, because the agent had no
`[jmap] vtc` switch. So a client could open the socket but could not call
VTCCall/signal to put anything into it.

NO END-TO-END PROOF YET: vtc_stream.rs has 3 unit tests, and nothing drives
a signal through a real socket to another agent. That is bead
mimid-1wgh.114.10, now unblocked.
